newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank says no need to change repo.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank says no need to change repo.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Monday it saw no need to change its key repurchase rate.

It forecast two percent growth this year and three percent next year, while it saw underlying inflation between 1.5 percent and two percent 1997 and 1998 and possibly into 1999, Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom said in a speech at a monetary policy seminar in Stockholm.
Growth will not threaten the Riksbank's inflation target of two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side, he said.
"The current boost to the economy means no threat to the price stability target at present," Backstrom said.
"The conclusion is therefore that there is no need to change the repo rate."
The Riksbank lowered the rate to 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent last year but has so far this year not moved the repo.
Despite stronger growth unemployment could remain high, Backstrom said.
"There is a risk that a large part of unemployment is structural," Backstrom said. "Thereby it risks remaining at a high level even when economic trends are better."
In April Swedish unemployment amounted to 8.3 percent, according to Statistics Sweden.
